summary: Brian Houghton Hodgson specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Haileybury, East India Company College, Fort William College, and under Amritananda Bandya. He served as Assistant Resident (1820–1843) and British Resident in Nepal (~1833–1843).

Brian J. Nichols works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He studied at Rice University (PhD ~2004–2011) and the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies under Anne Carolyn Klein and other scholars.

Bridget Allchin was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Cape Town. She founded the European Association of South Asian Archaeology and Art in 1970 and held a post at Wolfson College around 1977.
Brigitte Marschall studied at the University of Vienna from around 1976 to 1984. She later held a post there as Professorin around 2001.

Bronislaw Malinowski studied at Jagiellonian University, Leipzig University, and the London School of Economics under Charles Gabriel Seligman. He held posts at the London School of Economics (~1913–1938), Cornell University (~1933), and Yale University (~1939–1942).

Bronwyn Finnigan works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at the universities of Melbourne, Sydney, and Auckland, and held posts at the University of Auckland (~2009–2013), Marquette University (2012–2014), and the Australian National University (2014).

Brook Ziporyn works in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Chicago and the University of Michigan (PhD ~1988–1996 under Donald J. Munro), holding posts at Northwestern, National University of Singapore, and Chicago.
Brooke Schedneck is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Arizona State University (~2007–2012), studying under doctoral supervisor Juliane Schober.

Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his doctoral studies under Patricia Berger and Whalen Lai, alongside instruction from scholars including Michel Strickmann, Edward H. Schafer, and Lewis Lancaster.
Bruce Chilton works in religious studies. He studied at St John's College, Cambridge (~1973–1977), and later held posts at Yale University (~1985–1987) and Bard College (~1987).
Bruce John Stewart works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Sakya College in 1978 and earned a PhD from Columbia University by 1983 under the supervision of Alex Wayman.

Bruce Lincoln works in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Haverford College and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, later holding posts at the University of Minnesota and Chicago.

Bruce Matthews works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He pursued graduate studies at McMaster University (~1970–1974) and held posts at the University of Ceylon (~1968–1969) and Acadia University (~1976).
Bruce McCoy Owens works in religious studies and Indology. He held an academic post at Columbia University and served as associate professor of anthropology at Wheaton College around 1996.
Bruno Dagens was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Colette Caillat and served as a professor at KU Leuven from around 1977 to 1986.
Bruno Galasek specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Bonn by 2016 under doctoral supervisor Konrad Klaus.

Bruno Liebich worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Franz Kielhorn (~1882–1885) and held posts as Professor Ordinarius at the University of Breslau (1902) and at Heidelberg University (~1921–1934).
Bruno Lindner was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth from 1870 to 1879 and held a post at Leipzig University from around 1882 to 1924.
Bruno Lo Turco is an Indologist and philosopher. He completed his doctoral thesis at Sapienza University of Rome between 1997 and 1998 under the supervision of Raffaele Torella.

Bryan D. Lowe works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Otani University and under graduate advisor Jacqueline I. Stone, among others, later holding a post at Vanderbilt University (~2012–2019).
